title: From Three Directions, Among the Ansar • Entering with a Bowed Head • Inside the Ka‘bah • Standing at the Door of the Ka‘bah • The Adhan on the Roof of the Ka‘bah • An Exception to Forgiveness, and Restraint Within Forgiveness

blocks.0: From Three Directions, Among the Ansar
blocks.1: Reaching Dhu Tuwa the Prophet {{1}} drew up the army in ranks. The army would enter Makkah from three directions. On one side Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam (RA), on another Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA). With the infantry, Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah (RA) through the middle of the valley. The Prophet {{2}} himself was in one band. Seeing Abu Hurayrah (RA) in the distance he called, Abu Hurayrah! He said, at your service, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet {{3}} said, let no one come to me except an Ansari. Call the Ansar. The Ansar came and stood around the Prophet {{4}}. Meanwhile Quraysh gathered a rabble of its own. They thought, let us send these ahead. If they gain some advantage we will be with them. If they lose, we will give them whatever they want. The Prophet {{5}} saw them and said, do you see that band of Quraysh? Then, placing one hand over the other, he gestured, until you meet me at Safa. On Khalid’s (RA) path was Khandamah. There ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Safwan ibn Umayyah and Suhayl ibn ‘Amr had gathered to stop the Muslims. Himas ibn Qays of Banu Bakr had been making weapons for days on end. His wife had asked, who are these for? He had said, for Muhammad and his companions. His wife had said, by Allah, no one can stop them. He had said, I will make one of them your servant. There was a little fighting. Twelve of Quraysh were killed. The rest ran away. Safwan and ‘Ikrimah too. Two of the Muslims were martyred, Kurz ibn Jabir al-Fihri and Khunays ibn Khalid (RA), who had gone by a separate path from the main body and got lost. Himas returned home and told his wife, quickly bolt the doors and windows. His wife said, where has gone all that you were saying all this time? He said, if you had been there on the day of Khandamah, the day Safwan and ‘Ikrimah fled, you would not have rebuked me.{{6}}
blocks.2: The weapon made for the Prophet {{1}} and his companions was of no use on the field. Boasting with the mouth is easy. The weight is known when you stand face to face. And the hand that ran to stop the Prophet {{2}}, from that very hand in the end a pact of safety had to be asked.
blocks.4: Into the city from which eight years earlier he had had to leave, hidden, in the darkness of night, the Prophet {{1}} entered on camelback. Anas (RA) said, he entered Makkah with his chin resting on the howdah, bowed, in humility.{{2}}
blocks.5: And sitting on the camel he was reciting Surah al-Fath, drawing out the tune, repeating again and again.{{1}}
blocks.6: The surah in whose very beginning, about two years earlier, the Treaty of Hudaybiyah had been called a victory, on the day when many of the Companions could not understand it; today he enters Makkah reciting that same surah with his own mouth. At the moment of victory there is no proud announcement on his lips, there is the Qur’an; the head is not raised, it is bowed. What became of the Ka‘bah and the idols around it is told in Dars 2.
blocks.8: After finishing the tawaf the Prophet {{1}} called ‘Uthman ibn Talhah (RA), the keeper of the Ka‘bah’s key. He told him to bring the key. The door opened. But the Prophet {{2}} did not enter at once. Inside there were still idols and pictures. Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) said, the Prophet {{3}} refused to enter while there were gods inside. He gave the order, and they were brought out. Brought out too were the pictures of Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS), with divination arrows in their hands. The Prophet {{4}} said,
blocks.10: May Allah destroy them! They know very well that Ibrahim and Isma‘il never sought to learn fate with these arrows.{{1}}
blocks.11: Then he entered. With him were Usamah ibn Zayd, Bilal and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah (RA). The door was closed from inside. He spent a long time inside. In the corners of the house he said takbir. Then he prayed. When he came out Ibn ‘Umar (RA), entering first of all, saw Bilal (RA) standing beyond the door. He asked, did the Prophet {{1}} pray inside the Ka‘bah? Bilal said,
blocks.13: Yes, two rak‘ahs. Between the two pillars on the left as you enter.{{1}}
blocks.16: In the house that Ibrahim (AS) had raised for tawhid, pictures were drawn in his own name, with divination arrows in the hand. People love to carry on the work they like in the names of great people. The Prophet {{1}} first wiped out that false name, then entered. Even entering as a victor, he did not set foot inside without stopping the work that had been going on in the house. Today in our houses too such pictures exist. A deed that was not to the Prophet’s {{2}} liking, yet is carried on by invoking elders: the people before us used to do it. Before entering the house those pictures need to be taken down.
blocks.17: Standing at the Door of the Ka‘bah
blocks.18: Then the Prophet {{1}} stood at the door of the Ka‘bah. Below were the people of Makkah; those who had thrown stones, who had starved him in the Valley of Abu Talib, who had plotted murder, who had laid the Companions on hot sand and put stones on their chests. Everyone was waiting to see what would happen. He said takbir three times, then said,
blocks.20: There is no god but Allah, He is One. He has made His promise true, helped His servant, and alone defeated all the factions. Listen, every pride, every claim of blood and wealth of the Jahiliyyah is beneath these two feet of mine; except the service of the Ka‘bah and the duty of giving water to the pilgrims.{{1}}
blocks.21: The chain of revenge of Jahiliyyah went on across tribe after tribe; the son took revenge for the father’s blood, the grandson for the son’s. In one sentence that chain was pressed beneath the feet. Then he asked, O Quraysh, what do you think I will do with you? They said, something good; you are a kind brother, son of a kind brother. He said, go, you are free.{{1}}
blocks.22: Twenty years’ account in hand, the witness of every blow standing in front. Yet not a single name was taken up for judgement. Power coming into hand usually changes people; he did not change; the kindness that was there in the weak days of Makkah, on the day of victory too it remained.
blocks.23: The Adhan on the Roof of the Ka‘bah
blocks.24: The time of prayer came. By the Prophet’s {{1}} command Bilal (RA) climbed to the roof of the Ka‘bah and called the adhan. From the throat that once had Makkah’s hot sand and a stone on the chest, there floated Allahu akbar. Where for a thousand years the market of idols had been crowded, for the first time rang out the adhan of tawhid. In the courtyard of the Ka‘bah some Qurayshis were then sitting: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, ‘Attab ibn Usayd and al-Harith ibn Hisham. ‘Attab said, Allah has honoured my father Usayd, he did not have to hear this sound. al-Harith said, by Allah, if I knew he was on the truth, I would follow him. Abu Sufyan said, I will say nothing. If I make a sound these very pebbles will tell him. The Prophet {{2}} came to them and said, I have come to know all that you said. Then he told their words one by one. ‘Attab and al-Harith said, we bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah. By Allah, no one was with us who could have conveyed this to you.{{3}}
blocks.25: However much a word is whispered, to the One who is listening there is no difference between a whisper and a shout. No one had informed the Prophet {{1}}. We keep a wall standing between what we say in hiding and what we say openly. That wall in fact does not exist.
blocks.26: An Exception to Forgiveness, and Restraint Within Forgiveness
blocks.27: There was forgiveness. But not every crime went on the same scale. Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) said, on the day of the conquest of Makkah the Prophet {{1}} gave safety to everyone, except four men and two women. He named them too. One of those four was ‘Abdullah ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Sarh. Ibn Khatal was hanging on to the cloth of the Ka‘bah. Someone informed the Prophet {{2}}. He said, kill him. According to al-Rahiq, singing verses in satire of the Prophet {{3}} and the Muslims had been the work of him and his two slave-girls. ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh had hidden with ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (RA), his foster brother. When the Prophet {{4}} called the people to the pledge, ‘Uthman brought him along and stood him before the Prophet {{5}}. He said, O Prophet of Allah, take ‘Abdullah’s pledge. The Prophet {{6}} raised his head and looked. He held back his hand. Three times. Three times he refused to take it. After the third time he took the pledge. Then he turned to the Companions and said,
blocks.29: Was there not even one sensible man among you, who on seeing me withhold my hand from his pledge would have stood up and killed him? The Companions said, we did not know what was in your mind. Why did you not signal us with your eye? He said, it does not befit a prophet to have a deceit of the eyes.{{1}}
blocks.31: Forgiveness does not mean abolishing the law. And within the law too the path of forgiveness was open. ‘Uthman interceded, the Prophet {{1}} accepted, though late. But giving an order to kill someone by a hint, one thing on the tongue, another in the mind, this posture is not for the Prophet {{2}}. What is in the mind is on the tongue. Keeping this match is the hardest of all. About several others on the list there are small stories in history. ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl had fled on the road to Yemen. His wife asked the Prophet {{3}} for safety. The Prophet {{4}} granted it. The wife herself rushed and brought her husband back. ‘Ikrimah accepted Islam, and in his later life his Islam was very beautiful. Safwan ibn Umayyah’s name was not on the list. But out of fear he too had fled. He had decided to go by sea to Yemen via Jeddah. Just then ‘Umayr ibn Wahb (RA) reached him. The very ‘Umayr whom after Badr Safwan had sent to Madinah to kill the Prophet {{5}}, on the promise of taking responsibility for his debt and children. The hand that had gone with a knife was now asking the Prophet {{6}} for safety to save Safwan’s life. The Prophet {{7}} granted it. As a sign he gave his own turban, which had been on his head when he entered Makkah. Safwan returned. He said, give me two months’ time. The Prophet {{8}} said, you are given four months. Safwan accepted Islam later.{{9}}
blocks.33: In the list of death sentences announced, nine men. By al-Rahiq’s count four lost their lives, five were forgiven and came into Islam. Today we know which name ended up where, but that day being on the list did not mean being finished. The door of forgiveness was open even inside that list. We too make lists of people’s names: this one will never return, that one will never be right. Allah showed through His Messenger that a list is at best our reckoning. The real reckoning is in another’s hand.

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim 1780 (Abu Hurayrah (RA); sahih): the Prophet {{1}} gave Zubayr charge of one flank, Khalid the other flank, and Abu ‘Ubaydah the infantry (husar); they took the middle of the valley, the Prophet {{2}} in one battalion (katibah); the Prophet {{3}} said to Abu Hurayrah, let no one come to me except an Ansari, call the Ansar; Quraysh had gathered some riff-raff (awbash); the Prophet {{4}}, placing one hand over the other, said, until you meet me at Safa. Sirah-based part: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 659–661 (Khandamah: the gathering of ‘Ikrimah, Safwan and Suhayl; the dialogue and verses with Himas ibn Qays’s wife; twelve of Quraysh killed; Muslim martyrs Kurz ibn Jabir al-Fihri and Khunays ibn Khalid, who had gone by a separate path from the main body). This part is Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.1: al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 4419, 8101 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)); al-Hakim: sahih on the condition of Muslim; al-Dhahabi (Tarikh al-Islam 2/548): sahih. The narration ‘his beard was almost touching the middle of the howdah’ (Ibn Ishaq ← ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr) al-Albani called weak; in the dars the words of Anas (RA)’s sahih narration have been kept.
footnotes.2: Sahih al-Bukhari 4281, 5047; Sahih Muslim 794 (from ‘Abdullah ibn Mughaffal (RA); reciting Surah al-Fath on the she-camel’s back on the day of the conquest of Makkah, with tarji‘).
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari 4288 (‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA)): the Prophet {{1}}, coming to Makkah, refused to enter because there were idols inside the House, by his order they were brought out, brought out were the pictures of Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS), divination arrows in their hands; the Prophet {{2}} said, ‘May Allah destroy them! They know very well that they never sought fate with them.’ Then entering inside he said takbir in the corners of the house, did not pray (in Ibn ‘Abbas’s narration). In Bilal’s narration (Bukhari 397, 4289) he prayed two rak‘ahs; the word of the one who saw is preferred. Calling ‘Uthman ibn Talhah the keeper of the key and telling him to bring the key, entering with Usamah ibn Zayd, Bilal and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah (RA), spending a long time inside: Bukhari 4289 (Ibn ‘Umar (RA)).
footnotes.4: Sahih al-Bukhari 397 (Mujahid ← ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA): finding Bilal standing between the two doors he asked, did the Prophet {{1}} pray inside the Ka‘bah? Bilal said, yes, two rak‘ahs, between the two pillars on the left as you enter; then coming out he prayed two rak‘ahs in front of the Ka‘bah); Sahih al-Bukhari 4289 (Ibn ‘Umar (RA): I forgot to ask how many rak‘ahs he had prayed).
footnotes.5: Sahih al-Bukhari 4288 (‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA)): the Prophet {{1}}, coming to Makkah, refused to enter because there were idols inside the House, by his order they were brought out, brought out were the pictures of Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS), divination arrows in their hands; the Prophet {{2}} said, ‘May Allah destroy them! They know very well that they never sought fate with them.’ Then entering inside he said takbir in the corners of the house, did not pray (in Ibn ‘Abbas’s narration). In Bilal’s narration (Bukhari 397, 4289) he prayed two rak‘ahs; the word of the one who saw is preferred. Calling ‘Uthman ibn Talhah the keeper of the key and telling him to bring the key, entering with Usamah ibn Zayd, Bilal and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah (RA), spending a long time inside: Bukhari 4289 (Ibn ‘Umar (RA)).
footnotes.6: Sahih al-Bukhari 397 (Mujahid ← ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar (RA): finding Bilal standing between the two doors he asked, did the Prophet {{1}} pray inside the Ka‘bah? Bilal said, yes, two rak‘ahs, between the two pillars on the left as you enter; then coming out he prayed two rak‘ahs in front of the Ka‘bah); Sahih al-Bukhari 4289 (Ibn ‘Umar (RA): I forgot to ask how many rak‘ahs he had prayed).
footnotes.7: Sunan Abi Dawud 4588 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr (RA)); al-Albani: hasan; Shu‘ayb Arna’ut: the chain is sahih. The three takbirs and the part ‘He has made His promise true … alone defeated all the factions’ are in the text quoted in al-Albani’s Irwa’ al-Ghalil 7/256 (the chain is sahih); the account of speaking while standing on the steps of the Ka‘bah is in the narration of Musnad Ahmad as verified by Ahmad Shakir (the chain is sahih).
footnotes.8: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham, ‘Fath Makkah’ (the question to Quraysh at the door of the Ka‘bah and ‘idhhabu fa-antumu al-tulaqa’’). ⚠ The chain of these specific sentences is weak: al-Albani said, I did not find any sahih chain for it, it came as mu‘dal in Ibn Hisham (al-Ta‘liqat al-Radiyyah 3/475; Silsilah Da‘ifah 1163). It has been kept as a scene, not as evidence. But the incident of general forgiveness for the people of Makkah is itself established by a sahih chain: the safety announcement of Sahih Muslim 1780; and those who accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah were later called by the name ‘tulaqa’’ (the freed), as came in the narration of Hunayn (Sahih al-Bukhari 4337).
footnotes.9: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 664–665 (Ibn Ishaq’s narration). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence. A separate sahih chain for Bilal (RA)’s adhan on the roof of the Ka‘bah has not been verified in this dars; the incident of the adhan on the roof is touched in one line of Dars 1. ‘Attab ibn Usayd and al-Harith ibn Hisham accepted Islam later.
footnotes.10: Sunan Abi Dawud 4359 (from Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA); al-Albani: sahih), Mustadrak al-Hakim 4414 (sahih on the condition of Muslim); Sahih al-Jami‘ 2426 (al-Albani: ‘it does not befit a prophet to have a treachery of the eyes’: sahih). ‘Abdullah ibn Sa‘d was ‘Uthman (RA)’s foster brother.

Sirah-based part: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 665–667 (the list of nine men: ‘Abd al-‘Uzza ibn Khatal, ‘Abdullah ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Sarh, ‘Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, al-Harith ibn Nufayl ibn Wahb, Miqyas ibn Subabah, Habbar ibn al-Aswad, the two slave-girls of Ibn Khatal, Sarah; in one narration four were killed, the rest were forgiven; by Ibn Ishaq’s count eight men and six women; Fath al-Bari 8/11–12).
footnotes.13: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 666–668 (‘Ikrimah: fled on the road to Yemen, his wife Umm Hakim bint al-Harith asked for safety and herself went and brought him back; Safwan: his name was not on the list, fleeing in fear by way of Jeddah on the road to Yemen; when ‘Umayr ibn Wahb al-Jumahi asked for safety, the Prophet {{1}} gave him the turban from his head as a sign; when Safwan asked for two months’ time, he said, you are given four months; later accepted Islam). Mustadrak al-Hakim 5138 (the incident of ‘Ikrimah; the narrators are reliable, al-Haythami: its men are thiqah); the part ‘marhaban bi al-rakib al-muhajir’ of al-Hakim 5142 and al-Tirmidhi is munqati‘ (al-Dhahabi, al-Haythami), so it has not been brought into this dars. The earlier incident of ‘Umayr and Safwan is in Dars 15. Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.

quiz.q: What is understood about boasting with the mouth and the truth of the battlefield from the incident of Khandamah?
o: The door of forgiveness is open even inside the list
Boasting is easy with the mouth; the weight is known when one comes face to face
Even in the work of truth not everything is to be told to everyone
Entering with a bowed head is the etiquette of victory, a sign of humility
quiz.e: Himas made the most weapons, and also fled first of all.

quiz.q: In Anas’s (RA) narration, how did the Prophet ﷺ enter Makkah?
o: Chin on the howdah, in humility
On horseback, in armour, sword in hand
quiz.e: With his chin on the howdah, bowed, in humility.

quiz.q: Which surah was the Prophet ﷺ reciting on entering Makkah?
What do the recitation of Surah al-Fath and the bowed head at the moment of victory signify?
o: Victory is Allah’s, not for arrogance
He was cautious for fear of the enemy
He was expressing grievance against the people of Makkah
quiz.e: The Qur’an on the lips, the head bowed.

quiz.q: On a day of good exam results or promotion at work, what is the Prophet’s ﷺ example?
o: Holding a big event to show standing, so everyone knows
quiz.e: On the day of victory, the bowed head and the Qur’an.

quiz.q: What was in the hands of the pictures of Ibrahim and Isma‘il (AS) brought out from inside the Ka‘bah?
Which two duties were kept in force in the sermon at the door of the Ka‘bah?
o: Service of the Ka‘bah and giving water to the pilgrims
The duty of Quraysh’s old council

quiz.q: By what name were those who accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah later called?
‘Every claim of blood of the Jahiliyyah is beneath my feet’; what is the social significance of this?
o: Confiscation of all of Quraysh’s wealth
Breaking the chain of revenge from generation to generation
The decision to send all the leaders of Makkah into exile
quiz.e: The son used to take revenge for the father’s blood; that cycle ended.

quiz.q: Though the chain of the sentence ‘Go, you are free’ is weak, how is the incident of general forgiveness established?
o: It is not established in any way
Only in a line of poetry
Only in the speculation of later historians
In the safety announcement of Sahih Muslim
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 1780; and the name ‘tulaqa’’ is also proof.

quiz.q: The new generation too is carrying on an enmity from an old family dispute; what is the lesson of this dars?
o: Putting the old claims beneath the feet and ending it
Writing the dispute down so the next generation also does not forget
quiz.e: The Jahiliyyah claims of blood beneath the feet.

quiz.q: In the victory speech, first the praise of Allah, then settling old disputes; what is the application of this in a family reconciliation meeting?
o: Naming the guilty at the very start
Laying out the detailed account of everyone’s old wrongs
Gratitude at the start, then ending the old accounts
quiz.e: The order of the sermon at the Ka‘bah’s door.

quiz.q: The One from whom even hidden words are not concealed, whispering before Him; in which incident is this picture?
o: The incident of Safwan receiving the turban
The dialogue and verses with Himas’s wife
Abu Sufyan’s announcement of renewing the treaty
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ told their words one by one.

quiz.q: As a sign of safety for Safwan ibn Umayyah, what did the Prophet ﷺ give ‘Umayr ibn Wahb?
quiz.e: That turban which had been on his head when entering Makkah; Sirah-based.

quiz.q: After receiving safety, how many months’ time did Safwan ibn Umayyah ask for, and how many did he get?
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said, you are given four months.

quiz.q: In the incident of Ibn Abi Sarh, what does the statement ‘it does not befit a prophet to deceive with the eyes’ teach?
o: Keeping the head bowed even on the day of victory
Keeping dignity by making Abu Sufyan’s house a refuge
Breaking the fast on a journey and showing it before everyone
What is in the mind is on the tongue; no deceit by hints
